copper.usage: Action colour on the steel plate (dark, default).

copper-ink.usage: Text and icons on copper fills, dark theme.

iris-teal.usage: Second engraving ink: inner rosette, site mark, list ticks.

plate-steel.usage: Page ground, header, outline button fill, slip form panel.

plate-raised.usage: Single tonal lift: spec plate cells, contact section, footer, inputs, menus.

plate-accent.usage: Hover and highlight fill for outline, ghost, and menu items.

plate-border.usage: Every hairline rule and the spec plate grid gaps.

plate-input.usage: Input and outline-button borders; scrollbar thumb.

silver-ink.usage: Primary text, display name, engraved portrait fill.

silver-muted.usage: Secondary text and mono data labels.

engraving-line.usage: Main guilloché stroke: outer mesh, core, seals.

engraving-line-faint.usage: Medallion wave band, seal boundary ring.

microprint-silver.usage: Microprint text in rules and the medallion ring.

signal-red.usage: Field errors and invalid borders only.

copper-print-ink.usage: Text and icons on copper fills, light theme.

paper-muted.usage: Ground behind project screenshots, light theme.

paper-accent.usage: Hover and highlight fill, light theme.

paper-input.usage: Input and outline-button borders, light theme.

intaglio-blue.usage: Primary text and ink, light theme.

intaglio-blue-muted.usage: Secondary text and labels, light theme.

display.purpose: The name 'George Vlassis', once, full width at the foot of the hero. 22vw on phones, 21vw from 640px, min(13.4vw, 12.25rem) from 1024px; line-height 0.86 when broken over two lines, 0.98 inline.

statement.purpose: The single positioning sentence that opens the hero.

headline.purpose: Section headings (About, Experience, Projects, Contact). Balanced wrapping.

headline-sheet.purpose: Project names at the head of each project sheet.

title.purpose: Role titles in the experience record.

body-lead.purpose: Section ledes and narrative paragraphs, 36 to 62ch.

data-value.purpose: Values inside the hero spec plate.

control.purpose: Button and nav labels; large buttons use 1rem.

label.purpose: The data-label voice, uppercase: datasheet labels, list headings, captions, the slip address strip.

mono-data.purpose: Role date ranges, project addresses, social handles.

mono-meta.purpose: 'Stack:' lines with technologies joined by slashes.

microprint.purpose: Text inside microprint rules, uppercase, aria-hidden.

shadows.name: none
shadows.purpose: The system is flat. Depth comes from one tonal step (ground to raised plate), hairline rules, and solid overlap. The shadows on shadcn dropdown menus and sonner toasts are inherited library defaults, not part of the language.

motion.name: ease-expo
motion.purpose: The house ease for the engraving draw-in and the plate-press wipe (CSS var --ease-expo).

motion.name: engrave-draw
motion.purpose: The only entry animation: every guilloché pass in the medallion draws itself once on load. Drawn complete under reduced motion.

motion.name: plate-press
motion.purpose: Theme switch as one top-to-bottom wipe. Instant under reduced motion or without view transitions.

motion.name: latent-tilt
motion.value: rotate up to ±2.6deg, stroke-width 0.8 + 0.42 per degree, eased 9% per frame
motion.purpose: Turns the latent copy of the medallion mesh so the GV monogram surfaces as moiré; pointer on fine pointers, scroll on touch, static at 1.6deg under reduced motion.

motion.name: control-transition
motion.value: 200ms cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1) on background-color, border-color, color, box-shadow

narrative.overview:
The site is a document engineered not to be forged. Every decorative mark is a security feature drawn in code: guilloché rosettes woven from a single polar curve repeated at small rotations, microprint rules that carry real text, a line-engraved portrait, and a monogram hidden in the medallion's mesh that only surfaces when the plate is tilted. On top of that sits the discipline of a component datasheet. Proof is set as hairline spec rows with fixed label columns, never as cards. The engraving gives the page its authority, and the datasheet keeps it honest.

There are two physical states of the same object. Dark is the default: the steel intaglio plate, silver line work on near-black blue steel, with copper as the one warm metal. Light is the print pulled from that plate: intaglio-blue ink on cool green-grey security paper, with the copper deepened to a burnt print ink. The two themes are paired role for role, and switching between them runs the next plate through the press as a single top-to-bottom wipe.

Density is that of a document, not a dashboard. Sections breathe on generous vertical rhythm (96 to 160px), and type does the structural work: very large engraved display headings, quiet body text, and condensed mono labels for every datum. Anything that would feel like crypto hype (neon, glow, chain motifs, coins, currency marks) has been refused, and so have the centred name hero and rows of equal project cards. The security vocabulary is the antidote: it reads as rigor, not speculation.
keyCharacteristics: Code-generated guilloché, rosettes derived from real data (role start dates), drawn in two inks: line and iris.
Commissioner with its flare axis for engraved display type; Martian Mono only for data.
Hairline datasheet tables and 1px rules instead of cards, shadows, or filled panels.
Copper is the single action colour in both themes.
Near-square geometry: 2px corners on controls, square plates; the only curves are rosettes and perforations.
One entry animation (the engraving draw-in) and one transition (the plate-press theme wipe).

rules.name: The One Copper Rule
rules.body: Copper means "act". It appears on buttons that do something, links that lead to the contact slip, nav hover, focus, and selection, and nowhere else. It never strokes a rosette, colours a heading, or tints a surface.

rules.name: The Two Inks Rule
rules.body: Engraving uses only two inks: the line ink (silver or intaglio blue) and the iris ink. Both are translucent strokes that weave into the ground. Never fill an area with them, and never set body text in them.

rules.name: The Paired Plate Rule
rules.body: A colour token is not done until it exists in both `:root` (paper) and `.dark` (plate) with the same role. Dark is the default for first-time visitors, and light and system stay selectable.

rules.name: The Speak-or-Record Rule
rules.body: Commissioner speaks and Martian Mono records. Prose, headings, and buttons are never set in mono. Dates, labels, serials, handles, and stack lists are never set in Commissioner.

rules.name: The Flare Rule
rules.body: The flare axis is on (100) only for engraved type: display, statement, headline, and title, through the `font-engraved` utility. Body text always runs at flare 0. Volume rises with presence: 55 for the statement, 70 by default, 100 for the name alone.

rules.name: The Real Microprint Rule
rules.body: Microprint carries real, verifiable text: name, title, company, city, and domain, repeated. It is never lorem or filler, and it is always hidden from assistive technology because it is texture, not content.

rules.name: The Lattice Rule
rules.body: Nothing escapes the 88rem lattice except the medallion, which is allowed to bleed off the page edge, and the microprint rules, which run edge to edge.

rules.name: The Flat Plate Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat at rest and flat on hover. To separate a field, draw a hairline or step one tone up to the raised plate. Never lift it with a shadow.

dos: Do reserve copper (plate copper on dark, burnt print copper on light) for actions, the links that lead to the contact slip, nav hover, focus, and selection.
Do set every label, date, serial, handle, address, and stack list in Martian Mono through the `data-label` voice (0.6875rem, 0.08em tracking, uppercase, width 87.5) or the mono data sizes.
Do present specs as datasheet rows: a top hairline, a bottom hairline per row, a fixed mono label column, and 12 to 16px of vertical padding.
Do generate any new rosette from the guilloché helpers and real data. Stroke it in the line or iris ink at a non-scaling width between 0.4 and 1.1, and caption its parameters when it stands alone.
Do define every new colour token in both the paper and plate themes with the same role.
Do use engraved type (flare 100) for headings and statements, and keep body text at flare 0.
Do mount raster images in the double hairline frame (a 1px rule, a 6px inset, and a 1px rule).
Do give every motion a reduced-motion state that shows the finished drawing.
donts: Don't use cards: rounded, shadowed, or filled boxes that hold a summary. The shadcn Card and Badge primitives in the repo are not part of this system.
Don't add shadows to any surface, at rest or on hover.
Don't use neon, glow, chain motifs, coins, currency marks, or denominations. The security vocabulary is engraving and microprint, not crypto iconography.
Don't round structural plates, or round controls beyond 2px. Pill shapes are out. The only curves are the rosettes, rings, perforations, and the portrait's vignette.
Don't fill areas or set text in the line or iris inks. They are translucent strokes.
Don't set prose or headings in Martian Mono, or data in Commissioner.
Don't fill a microprint rule with placeholder or invented text.
Don't animate anything else on entry. The engraving draw-in is the page's one entrance, and the plate-press wipe is its one transition.
